name: GDPR — General Data Protection Regulation
description: Regulation (EU) 2016/679. Seeded with the articles that carry operative obligations for a SaaS controller or processor. Articles concerning supervisory authorities, remedies and delegated acts are deliberately omitted - they bind regulators and courts, not a tenant's control set, and listing them would inflate coverage percentages with nothing to implement.

sections.title: Chapter III — Rights of the data subject
Chapter V — Transfers to third countries

requirements.title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
requirements.text: Process personal data lawfully, fairly and transparently; for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes; limited to what is necessary; accurate; stored no longer than necessary; and with integrity and confidentiality. The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance (accountability).
requirements.guidance: Art.5(2) accountability is why a GRC record exists at all: the obligation is not merely to comply but to be able to demonstrate it.

requirements.title: Lawfulness of processing
requirements.text: Processing is lawful only if at least one of the six bases applies: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests.

requirements.title: Conditions for consent
requirements.text: Where consent is the basis, be able to demonstrate that consent was given; present consent requests clearly and distinguishably; allow withdrawal at any time as easily as it was given.

requirements.title: Processing of special categories of personal data
requirements.text: Processing of data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, genetic or biometric data for identification, health data, or data concerning sex life or sexual orientation is prohibited unless one of the Art.9(2) conditions applies.
requirements.guidance: Health data processed by an EMR falls here. Biometric identification of non-consenting individuals is the specific exposure flagged in the estate risk register.

requirements.title: Transparent information and modalities for exercising rights
requirements.text: Provide information and handle rights requests in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form; respond without undue delay and within one month of receipt, extendable by two further months for complex requests with notice to the subject.

requirements.title: Information to be provided where data is collected from the subject
requirements.text: At the time of collection, provide identity and contact details of the controller, purposes and legal basis, recipients, transfers, retention period, the subject's rights, and whether provision is mandatory.

requirements.title: Information to be provided where data is not obtained from the subject
requirements.text: Where personal data is obtained indirectly, provide equivalent information within a reasonable period and at the latest within one month, together with the source of the data.

requirements.title: Right of access
requirements.text: On request, confirm whether personal data is being processed and provide a copy together with the purposes, categories, recipients, retention period, rights, source and any automated decision-making logic.

requirements.title: Right to rectification
requirements.text: Rectify inaccurate personal data without undue delay and complete incomplete data, including by means of a supplementary statement.

requirements.title: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
requirements.text: Erase personal data without undue delay where one of the Art.17(1) grounds applies, and where the data has been made public take reasonable steps to inform other controllers processing it.

requirements.title: Right to restriction of processing
requirements.text: Restrict processing where accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful, the data is needed by the subject for legal claims, or an objection is pending verification.

requirements.title: Notification obligation regarding rectification, erasure or restriction
requirements.text: Communicate any rectification, erasure or restriction to each recipient to whom the data was disclosed, unless this proves impossible or disproportionate.

requirements.title: Right to data portability
requirements.text: Where processing is based on consent or contract and carried out by automated means, provide the data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and permit transmission to another controller.

requirements.title: Right to object
requirements.text: Cease processing on objection unless compelling legitimate grounds are demonstrated; cease immediately and unconditionally where the processing is for direct marketing.

requirements.title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
requirements.text: A subject has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them, save for the stated exceptions, with safeguards including human intervention.
requirements.guidance: Directly relevant to any AI-assisted clinical, credit or eligibility decision. The safeguard is meaningful human review, not a disclosure notice.

requirements.title: Responsibility of the controller
requirements.text: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and be able to demonstrate that processing is performed in accordance with the Regulation, reviewed and updated where necessary.

requirements.title: Data protection by design and by default
requirements.text: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures at the time of determining the means of processing and at the time of processing, and ensure that by default only personal data necessary for each specific purpose is processed.

requirements.title: Joint controllers
requirements.text: Where two or more controllers jointly determine purposes and means, determine their respective responsibilities in a transparent arrangement and make its essence available to data subjects.

requirements.title: Processor
requirements.text: Engage processors only under a contract setting out the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, obligations and rights; processors must not engage sub-processors without prior authorisation and must impose equivalent obligations on them.
requirements.guidance: This is the Data Processing Agreement, and the GDPR analogue of a HIPAA BAA. The sub-processor chain is the part most often left undocumented.

requirements.title: Records of processing activities
requirements.text: Maintain a record of processing activities including purposes, categories of subjects and data, recipients, third-country transfers, retention periods and a description of security measures; make it available to the supervisory authority on request.

requirements.title: Security of processing
requirements.text: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures having regard to the state of the art and the risk, including as appropriate pseudonymisation and encryption, ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, restoration of availability after an incident, and a process for regularly testing and evaluating effectiveness.

requirements.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
requirements.text: Notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless unlikely to result in a risk; a processor must notify its controller without undue delay. Document all breaches regardless of notifiability.
requirements.guidance: 72 hours, against HIPAA's 60 days. A single incident touching EU subjects and US PHI runs both clocks at once, and the shorter one governs the response plan.

requirements.title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
requirements.text: Where a breach is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, communicate it to affected subjects without undue delay, describing the nature of the breach, the contact point, likely consequences and measures taken.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.text: Carry out a DPIA prior to processing likely to result in a high risk, in particular for systematic and extensive automated evaluation, large-scale processing of special categories, or systematic monitoring of a publicly accessible area on a large scale.

requirements.title: Designation of a data protection officer
requirements.text: Designate a DPO where processing is carried out by a public authority, where core activities involve regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale, or where core activities involve large-scale processing of special categories of data.
requirements.guidance: Modelled as addressable because the duty is conditional: determine and document whether the triggers apply rather than assuming either way.

requirements.title: General principle for transfers
requirements.text: Transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation only where the conditions of Chapter V are met, and ensure the level of protection guaranteed by the Regulation is not undermined.

requirements.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
requirements.text: In the absence of an adequacy decision, transfer only where appropriate safeguards are provided, such as standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules or an approved code of conduct, together with enforceable rights and effective remedies for data subjects.
